newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil pension reform bill delayed another week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pension reform bill delayed another week.

text.p: The Brazilian government's pension reform bill faces at least another week's delay in a Senate committee as lawmakers continue to wrangle over its particulars, an official said Tuesday.

The bill is currently awaiting a vote in the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee. If approved there, it advances to the floor of the Senate where it requires two three-fifths majorities to pass muster.

The reform, which has been stuck in Congress for over two years, is considered pivotal to the government's effort to stem the red ink in the social security system and narrow Brazil's public sector deficit.

Progress is being held up by differences over several points in the reform, in particular an article that would end automatic increases in civil service pensions to match any pay rises to public sector workers, the official said.
"There is no way the bill is going to be voted on by the (Constitution and Justice Committee) this week," he said.
If approved in the Senate, the bill will have to return to the Chamber of Deputies for approval of changes made in the upper house.
Many analysts believe the government may not manage to get the reform through Congress before next year's elections, which are already beginning to overshadow the political scene.

The government's other flagship reform, of the civil service, is due to be put to a second full vote on the floor of the Chamber of Deputies either next week or early August. It also has to be approved in the Senate.
